documents.title: AI Syllabus Statements
documents.stance_why: The document sets no stance of its own: it offers 'Prohibited', 'Limited' and 'Integration Allowed' sample statements ('Example Syllabus Statements for MU Instructors'), so instructors choose, i.e. delegates with three tiers.
documents.summary: The Provost's sheet gives MU instructors three degrees of AI integration, with sample syllabus statements and citation examples borrowed from MU units and other universities. It shows the university's template language and leaves each instructor to choose.

units.why: The sheet sorts sample statements by 'Degree of AI Integration Permitted' into three named degrees, which is a tiered scheme for course AI policy, so P05.
units.anchor: Degree of AI Integration Permitted
units.frag_end: Find helpful icons for all AI positions
units.policy: The provost sheet sorts example syllabus statements into three degrees: AI usage prohibited, limited AI usage permitted, and AI integration allowed.

units.why: The intro tells instructors to 'Start with General Statements About AI Usage to communicate the extent to which AI use is permitted overall', guidance on building a syllabus policy, so P09 (state AI expectations in the syllabus).
units.anchor: Start with General Statements About AI Usage to communicate the extent
units.policy: Instructors should start their course AI policy with a general statement of the extent to which AI use is permitted overall.
units.fit_note: Frames the statement as a build step for instructors rather than a requirement to include one.

units.why: 'If AI is allowed to any degree, review examples of transparency guidelines' directs instructors to add citation and attribution practices; closest is P24 (disclosure) though it addresses instructors, not students.
units.anchor: review examples of transparency guidelines that describe citation and attribution practices
units.frag_start: If AI is allowed to any degree,
units.policy: Where AI is allowed to any degree, instructors review examples of transparency guidelines that describe citation and attribution practices.

units.why: The prohibited example says 'a strict policy against the use of AI software in any aspect of the learning process', a total ban, so P01.

units.policy: The course maintains a strict policy against the use of AI software in any aspect of the learning process.

units.why: Students must 'rely solely on their own cognitive abilities' when 'drafting, editing, and revising', which rules out AI even for editing or revision, so P21.

units.policy: The course policy is in place to uphold individual academic achievement and to ensure that assessments accurately reflect each student's independent learning and writing capabilities.

documents.title: What is the University of Missouri System's policy on student AI use?

documents.summary: The UM System page leaves the decision on student AI use to each instructor or department, with a default ban when an instructor does not clearly allow it. It adds a stoplight framework and advice on setting and communicating the policy.

documents.title: ChatGPT, Artificial Intelligence, and Academic Integrity
documents.stance_why: It says 'using ChatGPT on assignments is prohibited if the instructor does not allow its use' and that use 'without permission' is a violation: AI is banned unless the instructor permits it, so restrict.
documents.summary: The Office of Academic Integrity explains that using ChatGPT and similar tools without instructor permission or in improper ways violates the academic integrity rules. It quotes the August 2023 conduct language and advises students to ask first when unsure.

units.policy: ChatGPT and other AI products can be used for purposes both good and bad; there are legitimate ways to use these tools for research and ways to use them to cheat on academic work.
units.fit_note: Acknowledges legitimate uses and misuse without naming specific benefits.

documents.stance_why: The page says 'Academic units will create policies' and that units 'restrict all uses of AI, permit some uses of AI, or permit all uses of AI', so the decision goes to units, i.e. delegates, with three options as tiers.
documents.summary: The Graduate School requires academic units to write AI policies for coursework, supervised research, qualifying exams and capstones, with required elements. It sets no rule on whether AI is allowed.

units.why: 'Academic units will create policies related to the use of AI' across four areas puts rule-making with units, so P85.

units.policy: Academic units create policies on the use of AI that are relevant to their disciplines for organized coursework, supervised research, qualifying and comprehensive exams, and capstone experiences.

units.why: 'Each policy needs to include the following elements' lists the required contents (goals, whether AI is permitted, tasks and tools), so P09.
units.anchor: Each policy needs to include the following elements
units.policy: Each unit policy includes the goals of the educational experience, whether AI is permitted, and, if permitted, which tasks and tools are permitted.
units.fit_note: Applies to unit policies for coursework, research, exams and capstones, not only syllabi.

units.why: 'The goal(s) of the educational experience' must be stated, tying AI rules to objectives, so P83.
units.anchor: The goal(s) of the educational experience
units.policy: Each unit policy states the goals of the educational experience.
units.fit_note: Requires stating goals, not explicitly that AI rules follow from them.

units.why: 'how AI use should be disclosed and acknowledged' requires each unit policy to specify disclosure, so P24.
units.anchor: how AI use should be disclosed and acknowledged
units.policy: Where AI is permitted, each unit policy specifies how AI use should be disclosed and acknowledged.
units.fit_note: Requires units to specify disclosure rules; does not itself bind students.

units.policy: All policies created by academic units must be compliant with ethical, research, and IT guidelines from the University of Missouri and other relevant stakeholders, such as granting agencies and publishers.
